generation.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Correct ONE original flat TTE parasternal long-axis RV outflow illustration for Heart Explorer, ASE2019 Table2 row2.5. Input1 is the edit target and exact style reference. Input2 is the exact published row2.5 anatomy+echo crop, used ONLY for anatomical relationships; do not copy its pixels, labels, photographic texture or panel layout. Keep the ivory square canvas, gray sector, terracotta tissue, thin brown contours and bold black labels of Input1. Preserve RVOT above/anterior, PA downstream toward display-right/lower-right, LV lower-left and LA lower-right. CRITICAL REPAIRS: Delete the two isolated brown tendinous-looking strokes in LV. At the LV–LA junction, remove the broad terracotta bridge that currently seals LA from LV: that location in the source is the oblique MITRAL ANNULUS, not a muscular partition. Represent it with two thin pale MITRAL leaflet profiles, each fixed to one annular margin, meeting centrally as a CLOSED valve during systole. No muscle across the annular orifice, no floating leaflets, no chordae. Keep the LA free wall as a complete THIN terracotta ribbon with inner and outer brown boundaries, except the real mitral junction; LV myocardium remains much thicker. Use a coherent SYSTOLIC EJECTION frame: PV OPEN, MV CLOSED. At PV, ventricular side is RVOT upper-left and arterial side is PA lower-right. Draw exactly two visible thin semilunar cusp profiles hinged to opposing root margins and displaced toward the PA walls; their free ends extend downstream into PA. Leave a broad unmistakable central white RVOT→PA outflow channel. Do not use a coapting tent-shaped AV-valve symbol or globally flip a W. PA side walls remain thin filled vascular ribbons, not muscle slabs. Exact labels: RVOT in upper pool, PA in downstream artery, LV in lower-left ventricular pool, LA in lower-right atrium, PV with a short leader ending directly on one pulmonary cusp. All labels clear at200px. No other labels, no new chamber, no PA–LA or Ao–PA connection, no extra valve, no chord, no aortic root in this focused plane, no title or watermark. Preserve all other geometry and the source-supported oblique mitral relationship. ONE square output.

generation.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Make one precise repair to the provided original Heart Explorer TTE illustration, apical four-chamber RV-focused view (ASE comprehensive TTE2019 Table2 row2.16). Input1 is both the edit target and exact style reference. Keep its square canvas, gray sector, chamber shapes, normal LV-forming apex, complete smaller RV, thick LV/septum versus thinner RV, positions, all four bold labels, and both open attached atrioventricular valves. The only anatomical correction is the atrial tissue: the RA and LA currently have ivory strips between their brown inner and outer outlines, so their walls appear empty. Fill these existing narrow free-wall strips with the SAME muted terracotta as myocardium, and fill the thin interatrial septal tissue. Preserve distinct inner and outer contours. Their thin colored wall band must remain perceptible at a 200px gallery size, about1–3px there, while clearly thinner than ventricular myocardium. This is actual atrial tissue, not a new external outline. Preserve the open white MV and TV inflow paths and the thin pale leaflets with their original annular attachments. Do not fill any valve orifice or leaflet with muscle. Do not enlarge either atrium, do not introduce ASD or extra cavities, do not move the RV apex beyond the LV apex. Exact existing labels: RV upper-left, LV upper-right, RA lower-left, LA lower-right. Keep bold dark sans-serif typography and generous clearance. Opaque ivory background and lumens; terracotta tissue; thin brown contours; no gradients, texture, 3D, titles, angle dials, UI frame or watermarks. Output ONE square final illustration with only the bounded tissue-fill correction.

Do not invent a separate RA pool: the exact 2.17a reference does not display one. Exact labels: RV in RV, LV in LV, LA in LA, LVOT pointing to the outflow, Ao in aorta, and add AV with a short leader ending on an aortic cusp, clear of the LVOT leader. Bold dark sans-serif labels with room around glyphs. Preserve all other proportions and anatomy. No extra panels, title, scanner text, watermark, gradients or decorative detail. initial_audit.repair_prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Make one square, production-quality scientific educational illustration. Image 1 is the current Heart Explorer edit target and style anchor. Image 2 is the exact ASE 2013 Table 10 source view for plane/anatomical orientation only, not a style to copy. Preserve the ivory background and blood pools, muted terracotta tissue, fine dark-brown contours, gray sector, and bold black sans-serif labels. Keep the same sector orientation, composition, chamber locations and crop; change only the items specified. Every visible muscular wall must have a finite terracotta ribbon with two crisp interfaces, thinner for atrium/RV than LV. Keep true valve leaflets, chordae, membranous septum and aorto-mitral curtain slender; do not convert fibrous tissue into myocardium. Two brown outlines with ivory blood-colored fill are not enough for a muscular free wall. Sector crops are intentional; do not close a cropped cavity with a cap. No invented vessels, tumors, thrombi, chordae, semilunar chordal attachments, duplicated tubes, extra leaflet count, or unlabeled principal cavity. Major labels must remain readable at 200px. Output only the illustration, no title, caption, panel lettering or source screenshot. TEE ME five-chamber (ASE view1). Add continuous thin terracotta RA and LA free-wall ribbons, following their existing outside contours and ending only at sector cuts/valve annuli. Keep four chamber lumens and RV/LV septum in place. Preserve the central LVOT from LV toward the small upper aortic profile. Do not turn a short 2D aortic section into a long invented tube. Depict normal ventricular ejection: MV and TV gently coapted on the ventricular side of their annuli; two thin AV cusp profiles opened apart toward their aortic walls with a clearly visible central opening. The aortic/ventricular sides must remain correct. Add a small AV label with short precise leader to a cusp; preserve RA, LA, RV, LV and LVOT labels. Do not cover the AV with text.

generation.prompt:
Perform a narrowly localized medical illustration correction on the supplied Heart Explorer ME long-axis TEE image. Retain its square ivory background, gray sector, dark-brown contours, terracotta tissue, label typography and all chamber geometry. The image is a source-reviewed ASE 2013 Table 10 view 5 plane. The required phase is normal ventricular ejection: MV remains closed; AV is open. This is a local anatomical edit, not a redesign.

Use the supplied image as the target, especially its intact upper and lower aortic wall ribbons. Preserve the continuous artery walls behind the valve, as TWO separate uninterrupted terracotta ribbons reaching the right sector boundary. Preserve the entire closed RV roof under the aortic root. Leave the LA muscular wall, thin closed MV, LV myocardium and septum, LVOT, Ao, RV and every label unchanged.

ONLY correct the two pale aortic cusp profiles lying inside the aortic root: presently their downstream ends join the wall, resembling attached lenses. initial_audit.repair_prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Make one square, production-quality scientific educational illustration. Image 1 is the current Heart Explorer edit target and style anchor. Image 2 is the exact ASE 2013 Table 10 source view for plane/anatomical orientation only, not a style to copy. Preserve the ivory background and blood pools, muted terracotta tissue, fine dark-brown contours, gray sector, and bold black sans-serif labels. Every visible muscular wall must have a finite terracotta ribbon with two crisp interfaces, thinner for atrium/RV than LV. Keep true valve leaflets, chordae, membranous septum and aorto-mitral curtain slender; do not convert fibrous tissue into myocardium. Two brown outlines with ivory blood-colored fill are not enough for a muscular free wall. Sector crops are intentional; do not close a cropped cavity with a cap. No invented vessels, tumors, thrombi, chordae, semilunar chordal attachments, duplicated tubes, extra leaflet count, or unlabeled principal cavity. Major labels must remain readable at 200px. Output only the illustration, no title, caption, panel lettering or source screenshot. TEE modified bicaval tricuspid view (ASE view12). Make the existing RA free-wall ribbon a thin continuous terracotta muscular band, joining existing RV/annular tissue smoothly but not blocking the TV. attempts.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Make one square, production-quality scientific educational illustration. Image 1 is the current Heart Explorer edit target and style anchor. Image 2 is the exact ASE 2013 Table 10 source view for plane/anatomical orientation only, not a style to copy. Preserve the ivory background and blood pools, muted terracotta tissue, fine dark-brown contours, gray sector, and bold black sans-serif labels. Keep the same sector orientation, composition, chamber locations and crop; change only the items specified. Every visible muscular wall must have a finite terracotta ribbon with two crisp interfaces, thinner for atrium/RV than LV. Keep true valve leaflets, chordae, membranous septum and aorto-mitral curtain slender; do not convert fibrous tissue into myocardium. Two brown outlines with ivory blood-colored fill are not enough for a muscular free wall. Sector crops are intentional; do not close a cropped cavity with a cap. No invented vessels, tumors, thrombi, chordae, semilunar chordal attachments, duplicated tubes, extra leaflet count, or unlabeled principal cavity. Major labels must remain readable at 200px. Output only the illustration, no title, caption, panel lettering or source screenshot. TARGETED LABEL EDIT ONLY to TEE left atrial appendage view (ASE view15). Keep the full existing LA-LAA geometry, finite terracotta appendage wall, open appendage neck, blind distal appendage end, and upper-right ridge/venous context exactly. Add LUPV with a short fine leader into the small upper-right pulmonary-vein blood-pool region, to the right of the slender ridge, using nearby empty sector space so the existing small ostium is not covered. Preserve LA and LAA labels. Do not add pectinate muscles, thrombus-like bumps, a venous valve, extra branches, or an artificial roof; no geometric anatomical edits are needed.
